clue.text: House gets money owing back for nursery

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for money owing from right to left

parts.note: money owing is a debt

explanation.surface: A household falls into arrears, and the debt seems to fall on the children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' suggests children, but here it is a gardener's bed for raising young plants; 'back' is the reversal signal on the debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a heated bed of soil for raising young plants, which is what a garden nursery does.

clue.text: I got up to receive the king — a terrible person

indicators.note: the reversed self takes the king's letter inside it
in a down entry, got up means the word goes upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, the self
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: I rose to greet the monarch, a dreadful man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got up' reverses EGO to OGE, and 'to receive' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monster of folk tales, used of a cruel or frightening person.

clue.text: One tap bar drunk may think himself Napoleon

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone after one drink at the bar fancies himself the French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ONETAPBAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor; the surname identifies him.

clue.text: Give fellow a note

parts.note: a don is a university fellow
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Hand a man a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give something, especially to a cause.

clue.text: The problem of race?

parts.note: read not as a social issue but as something a runner must clear in a steeplechase-style event named after such barriers

explanation.surface: A grave question about racial issues.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests racial tension; the race is a sporting one in which competitors clamber over barriers.
explanation.definitionFit: Each barrier in that kind of race is a hurdle to get past, the very problem the clue names.

clue.text: Timothy and Helen, two combining in aria

indicators.note: the words are combined and their letters mixed together

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Timothy and Helen, a couple singing a duet in an opera song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combining' rearranges TIMOTHY, HELEN and TWO; 'two' in the surface counts the singers but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The English title of the clown's lament from Leoncavallo's opera Pagliacci, a famous tenor aria.

clue.text: How bookies pay place money?

parts.note: a spot is a place
cash is money

explanation.surface: How betting shops settle a bet placed each way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place money' looks like a racing bet that pays on a placing, but it is two synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers pay winners in ready cash on the spot, immediately.

clue.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

definitions.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

parts.words: On which adders slide to and fro?
parts.note: adders read not as snakes but as people adding up, sliding beads along wires

explanation.surface: A question about snakes slithering back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adders' suggests snakes; read it as people who add, moving beads on counting frames.
explanation.definitionFit: These counting frames with sliding beads are used for arithmetic, the plural of a Latin-derived word.

clue.text: He turns on a spider, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a bowler in cricket who makes the ball turn from the leg (or on) side
humorously, a creature with legs that spins webs

explanation.surface: A man who attacks a spider.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side; this type of bowler spins the ball from it. A spider is a spinner with legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler turning the ball from leg; and jokingly a web-spinning creature with many legs.

clue.text: Freshly minted trademark three quarters finished

parts.note: a brand is a trademark
three of the four compass quarters: north, east and west

explanation.surface: A newly struck trademark is three quarters of the way to completion.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass has four quarters (N, E, S, W); three of them give N, E, W. 'finished' rounds off the surface as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something freshly minted, like a new coin, is completely new and unused.

clue.text: Royal house, divided internally, naturally

definitions.meaning: the House of ... is the Dutch royal dynasty
a citrus fruit whose flesh grows in segments, split up inside by nature

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty torn apart by internal feuding, as one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a quarrelling dynasty; the second sense is the fruit, naturally split into segments.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch royal family is the House of Orange, and the citrus fruit has natural segments inside.

clue.text: Oscar's tiptop variety of bar snack

indicators.note: a variety is an assortment, signalling that the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: here the apostrophe-s supplies its letter S as part of the fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excellent type of snack served at Oscar's bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges OSCARS plus TIPTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Packets of crisps (US chips) are a staple snack sold in British pubs.

clue.text: A tenor isn't out to be loud

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer who is not out of tune is loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ATENORISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a Greek herald with a huge voice, so the adjective means very loud.

clue.text: Big name in the performing arts

indicators.note: the word arts is made to perform tricks, rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure in theatre, music and dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing arts' looks like a set phrase, but 'performing' is the anagram signal on ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A big name is a famous person, a celebrity or leading performer.

clue.text: It's slung out when scrapping

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their places and reordered

explanation.surface: Something is hurled aside during a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ITSSLUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapping in the sense of fighting is wrestling or grappling with someone.

clue.text: Cobbler's farewell ceremony?

parts.note: a shoemaker works on foot-shaped forms called lasts, so a cobbler's rituals would involve them

explanation.surface: A send-off for a retiring shoemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The sacrament given to the dying is read as rites performed with a cobbler's wooden foot forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacrament given to the dying is a farewell ceremony, and a cobbler's tools are lasts.

clue.text: The Scriptures completely recorded, it's reported

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: completely is wholly, and recorded is writ, old past participle of write

explanation.surface: The Bible was entirely written down, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's reported' turns WHOLLY WRIT into its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred writings, the Bible, are referred to as holy writ.

clue.text: Again, but for the last time?

definitions.meaning: the phrase used to mean one final go, as in a final repetition

explanation.surface: Repeat it, but this will be the final time.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase means simply 'again' and, in a phrase like 'one final go', a last repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a further repetition, and is often said of a final attempt before stopping.

clue.text: Slough's outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to slough is to cast off, as a snake does its skin
a small hut in a garden

explanation.surface: A building in Slough, the Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, but here it is the verb meaning to cast off skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast off skin is to slough it, and a garden hut is a small outbuilding.

clue.text: Revised point I'd raised with Edward

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters go upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward and I made a point that was then amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A revised text has been corrected or amended, which is to say edited.

clue.text: Party under cover?

parts.note: party in its legal sense of a person in a contract, and cover in the sense of insurance protection

explanation.surface: A secret gathering held undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration and 'under cover' secrecy; in insurance a party is a person and cover is protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has taken out insurance is a party protected by its cover.

clue.text: Perfect way to make a hole

definitions.text: Perfect way to make a hole

parts.words: Perfect way to make a hole
parts.note: in golf, finishing a hole with a single stroke is the perfect result

explanation.surface: The ideal method of digging a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a hole' suggests digging; in golf, a hole is completed in one stroke at best.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer who holes the ball with the first shot scores a hole in one, the perfect stroke.

clue.text: Roman day that is endless

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A day in Rome that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: ID EST loses its last letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell mid-month, as on the 15th of March.

clue.text: Potency of port half an hour later

indicators.note: later places the half-word after the port

parts.note: Vigo is a port in north-west Spain

indicators.note: half of the word hour, here its second half

explanation.surface: Port wine reaches full strength after thirty minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink, but it is the Spanish port VIGO; the second half of HOUR gives UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency means strength or power, and vigour is energetic strength.

clue.text: Such tolerance may be a matter of degree

definitions.text: Such tolerance may be a matter of degree

parts.words: Such tolerance may be a matter of degree
parts.note: tolerance as freedom of action, and degree as the unit in which distance from the equator is measured

explanation.surface: How much leeway is allowed varies with circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a matter of degree' sounds like 'it depends', but degrees literally measure angular distance north or south of the equator.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means freedom or leeway, and also a geographical position measured in degrees.

clue.text: Tyres can burst in race

indicators.note: burst suggests the letters fly apart and land in a new order

explanation.surface: During a motor race, tyres may blow out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst' rearranges TYRESCAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A race in the sense of a people or line of descent is one's family lineage.

clue.text: Neglect order issued

indicators.note: order as a verb, put into a new arrangement, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command is given to ignore something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges ISSUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect as a noun is a state of not being used or looked after.
